title: AgentBridge — Turn any CLI tool into an MCP server in 5 lines
problem: Developers waste hours wrapping CLI tools (e.g., ffmpeg, pandoc, sqlite3) as MCP servers for AI agents. Existing solutions require complex boilerplate or manual API design.
solution: A Python CLI that auto-generates an MCP server from any command-line tool. Just point it at a binary (or script) + describe its I/O, and it creates a persistent MCP server with tool discovery, streaming output, and error handling. Built with `subprocess`, `pydantic`, and `mcp` library.
target_market: Python developers, DevOps engineers, AI agent builders who need to integrate CLI tools (e.g., data scientists using `duckdb`, designers using `figma-cli`, or sysadmins using `kubectl`).

title: AgentOS — Local-first AI agent operating system
problem: AI agents lack a standard OS-like layer for persistence, scheduling, and inter-agent communication. Most agents are ephemeral scripts or rely on cloud services, making them unreliable for long-running tasks (e.g., research, automation).
solution: A lightweight Python framework that turns any agent into a persistent, schedulable service. Features: (1) Built-in SQLite database for agent memory/state, (2) Cron-like scheduling for tasks, (3) Inter-agent messaging via local sockets, (4) CLI for managing agents (`agentos start`, `agentos logs`). Includes a dashboard for monitoring agent health.
target_market: Developers building autonomous agents for research, automation, or business workflows. Startups and enterprises running agentic systems.

title: SkillSwarm — Crowdsourced AI agent skills marketplace
problem: AI agents are useless without skills (e.g., 'scrape Reddit', 'generate SQL queries'). Most developers reinvent the wheel or rely on brittle GitHub repos. There’s no centralized, trusted place to share, rate, and version-control skills.
solution: A lightweight CLI + web dashboard where users can publish, fork, and rate AI agent skills (e.g., MCP servers, Python scripts, or Claude Skills). Skills are tagged by use case (e.g., 'web-scraping', 'data-cleaning') and versioned. Includes a `skills install` command to auto-download and integrate skills into local agents.
target_market: AI agent builders, startups, and enterprises running autonomous agents. Open-source contributors and hobbyists.

title: TokenTamer — Real-time LLM token budget dashboard
problem: Developers building AI agents have no visibility into token usage until it’s too late. Cloud APIs (e.g., Mistral, OpenAI) provide no granular breakdown, leading to budget overruns or agent failures mid-task.
solution: A local proxy that intercepts all LLM API calls (via `httpx` middleware) and logs token usage per agent/skill/task in real-time. Provides a CLI dashboard (`tokentamer watch`) showing live token burn, cost estimates, and alerts when thresholds are hit. Supports Mistral, Ollama, and OpenAI APIs.
target_market: Startups, indie hackers, and enterprises running autonomous agents. Developers prototyping agent workflows.

title: AgentBridge — Turn any CLI into an AI agent in 30 seconds
problem: Developers waste hours wrapping CLI tools (git, ffmpeg, docker) for AI agents. Existing solutions require heavy frameworks or manual MCP server setup.
solution: A Python CLI tool that auto-generates MCP servers from any command-line tool. Just point it at your binary/script and it creates a persistent agent-ready interface with built-in error handling, streaming output, and tool discovery.
target_market: Backend engineers, DevOps teams, and AI tool builders who need to expose legacy CLI tools to agents without rewriting them

title: TokenTamer — Real-time LLM cost/latency dashboard
problem: Developers have no visibility into token economics of their AI agents. API costs explode silently while performance degrades.
solution: A background daemon that intercepts all LLM calls (local or API) and streams metrics to a web dashboard. Shows per-agent token usage, cost breakdowns, latency percentiles, and suggests optimizations (caching, model switching). Works with any agent framework via simple proxy.
target_market: Startups running production AI agents, freelance developers optimizing costs, research teams tracking experiments

title: AgentOS — Local-first agent orchestration kernel
problem: Running multiple agents (coding, research, automation) requires separate setups. No standard way to coordinate them or share state.
solution: A Rust-based daemon that runs on your machine as a system service. Manages agent lifecycles, shared memory, and tool permissions. Includes a CLI to launch/stop agents, monitor resource usage, and share tools between them. Agents communicate via simple JSON-RPC over Unix sockets.
target_market: Power users running multiple AI agents, research teams, and companies building agent platforms

title: AutoMCP — Self-hosted MCP server orchestrator
problem: AI agents need multiple MCP servers (e.g., for filesystem, browser, APIs), but managing them is a nightmare. Existing solutions require manual setup, port conflicts, or brittle Docker configs. No easy way to auto-discover and load MCP servers dynamically.
solution: A lightweight daemon that auto-discovers and loads MCP servers from a local directory (or GitHub). Provides a unified MCP endpoint for agents, with built-in health checks, auto-restart, and logging. Includes a `automcp start` CLI to spin up servers on demand. Built with `mcp`, `httpx`, and `watchfiles` for hot-reloading.
target_market: AI agent developers, DevOps teams, and power users running local agents. Teams using tools like Claude Code or Cursor.

title: SkillSwarm — Collaborative agent skill marketplace
problem: AI agents are siloed - skills (tools, knowledge) aren't shareable across teams/projects. Developers rebuild the same skills repeatedly.
solution: A lightweight peer-to-peer skill registry where agents can publish/consume skills as GitHub repos. Includes versioning, dependency resolution, and a CLI to install skills into any agent framework (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.). Skills are just Python modules with standardized interfaces.
target_market: AI-first startups, research labs, and enterprise teams building multi-agent systems

title: ContextCraft — Zero-setup codebase indexing for agents
problem: Agents struggle with large codebases because they lack proper context. Existing solutions require complex setup (embeddings, vector DBs).
solution: A Python CLI that creates a lightweight, always-up-to-date codebase index in SQLite. Uses AST parsing to track dependencies, functions, and classes. Agents query it via a simple MCP server. Updates incrementally as files change. No external services needed.
target_market: Solo developers and small teams using AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor) on large codebases
